_about: Historical stress windows (dates are historical facts: US market sessions). anchor='start_close' measures from the close ON the start date (peak-to-trough windows); anchor='prior_close' measures from the close of the session BEFORE the start date, so the start day's move is included. P&L uses real prices fetched for the window; nothing here is a price or a return.

scenarios.name: Black Monday
scenarios.description: Selling from 14 Oct culminated in the 19 Oct 1987 crash, the largest one-day percentage fall of the S&P 500 and the Dow.

scenarios.name: Russia default / LTCM
scenarios.description: Russia devalued and defaulted on 17 Aug 1998; LTCM's collapse and flight to quality followed until the Fed-brokered recapitalisation and rate cuts in early October.

scenarios.name: Dot-com bust
scenarios.description: S&P 500 peak close on 24 Mar 2000 to its bear-market closing low on 9 Oct 2002.

scenarios.name: 9/11 reopening
scenarios.description: US equity markets closed after the 11 Sep 2001 attacks and reopened on 17 Sep; measured from the last close before the closure to the 21 Sep low.

scenarios.name: Global Financial Crisis
scenarios.description: S&P 500 record close on 9 Oct 2007 to the crisis closing low on 9 Mar 2009.

scenarios.name: Lehman week
scenarios.description: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 Sep 2008; AIG rescue, money-fund 'break the buck' and the short-selling ban followed that week.

scenarios.name: Flash crash
scenarios.description: Intraday collapse and rebound of US equities on 6 May 2010; daily close-to-close move (the intraday trough is not visible in daily data).

scenarios.name: US downgrade
scenarios.description: Debt-ceiling standoff and S&P's downgrade of the US to AA+ (5 Aug 2011), followed by the 8 Aug sell-off.

scenarios.name: Taper tantrum
scenarios.description: Bernanke's 22 May 2013 testimony signalling QE tapering triggered a sharp rise in Treasury yields and a cross-asset sell-off.

scenarios.name: China devaluation
scenarios.description: PBoC devalued the renminbi on 11 Aug 2015; global equities fell into the 24-25 Aug sell-off.

scenarios.name: Brexit referendum
scenarios.description: UK voted to leave the EU on 23 Jun 2016 (results after the US close); markets sold off on 24 and 27 Jun.

scenarios.name: Volmageddon
scenarios.description: S&P 500 record close on 26 Jan 2018; the 5 Feb VIX spike wiped out short-volatility ETPs, and equities bottomed on 8 Feb.

scenarios.name: Q4 2018 sell-off
scenarios.description: S&P 500 record close on 20 Sep 2018 to the Christmas Eve low, on Fed tightening and trade-war fears.

scenarios.name: COVID crash
scenarios.description: S&P 500 record close on 19 Feb 2020 to the pandemic closing low on 23 Mar 2020.

scenarios.name: 2022 inflation bear market
scenarios.description: S&P 500 record close on 3 Jan 2022 to the 12 Oct 2022 closing low as the Fed hiked aggressively; stocks and bonds fell together.

scenarios.name: SVB / regional banks
scenarios.description: Silicon Valley Bank's 8 Mar 2023 capital-raise announcement, run and failure (10 Mar), Signature Bank's closure and regional-bank contagion.

scenarios.name: Yen carry unwind
scenarios.description: BoJ hike on 31 Jul 2024 and a weak US payrolls report triggered a yen-carry unwind; the Nikkei fell 12% and the VIX spiked on 5 Aug.
